variants.neutral: Arin wakes at the edge of town and steps out into the thin morning light, pockets empty but curiosity full.
variants.happy: Arin wakes with a skip in his step, humming a tune as he ties his boots and greets the day with a grin.
variants.uplift: Arin wakes to distant music — a festival is being set up. Today might hold an unexpected encounter.
variants.sad: Arin wakes slowly, the cobbles feel colder. He takes a breath and resolutely steps toward the town.

variants.neutral: He wanders into the market where stalls smell of spice and wood; merchants call softly as they arrange wares.
variants.happy: He bargains with a laughing spice-seller, trading a joke for a bright orange pouch that smells of sun.
variants.uplift: A traveling minstrel sings a strange melody; Arin catches a line that feels like a clue to something waiting.
variants.sad: A stall owner nods kindly but is busy; Arin buys a single apple and watches children dart between crates.

variants.neutral: At the square he meets a woman with ink-stained fingers who sketches maps for a small guild.
variants.happy: She gifts him a folded map with a flourish; their shared smile feels like the start of a friendship.
variants.uplift: She points to a hidden lane on the map and whispers of a rooftop garden that appears only at dusk.
variants.sad: She apologizes—her orders keep her busy—but she presses a tiny scrap of paper into his palm as a small comfort.

variants.neutral: A narrow lane leads to a creaking library whose windows hold dust-motes and quiet secrets.
variants.happy: Inside, an old librarian remembers him and hands over a bound folktale, nodding as if passing a torch.
variants.uplift: A loose page flutters from a book and lands on a sketch of an odd symbol; Arin tucks it away like a promise.
variants.sad: The librarian closes a heavy volume and tells a gentle story of distant places; Arin listens and feels oddly steadied.

variants.neutral: The hidden lane opens onto a rooftop garden where lanterns sway above the sleeping town.
variants.happy: Arin laughs as the garden lights flicker on one by one, as if the rooftops themselves were celebrating.
variants.uplift: Wind catches the lanterns and the whole garden hums; Arin feels the town hold its breath around him.
variants.sad: The garden is quiet and a little wild; Arin sits among the herbs and lets the town's murmur settle him.

callbacks.text: The guild map had marked this garden with a tiny star.

variants.neutral: Along the river stands a smith's workshop with copper bells and the smell of coal and iron.
variants.happy: The smith shows Arin a small, polished pendant and affixes it to his cord—'For luck,' he says, winking.
variants.uplift: A bell rings strangely overhead; the smith beckons to the quay and points to a tiny boat with painted stars.
variants.sad: The smith hums a low tune as he works; Arin watches the steady hammer and feels a quiet warmth in his chest.

variants.neutral: At the hillock he sees a small cottage with a crooked chimney and smoke like memory curling skyward.
variants.happy: An old friend appears on the porch, arms wide; they trade stories and a flask of warm tea.
variants.uplift: A child runs out clutching a paper kite that catches the wind and pulls Arin toward a hill where glimmers gather.
variants.sad: The cottage windows are dim; a neighbor waves sadly but offers a slice of bread and a short tale that comforts.

callbacks.text: A small cottage was inked on the map, right where he stands.
From the window he can see smoke curling up from the smith's chimney.

variants.neutral: Dusk finds him at a lantern-lit bridge where travelers pass with bags and hopeful eyes.
variants.happy: He helps a tired merchant carry a crate and is rewarded with a soft, grateful laugh and a new companion.
variants.uplift: Fireflies gather in a drift along the rails—each one a little compass leading him to a strange, bright gate.
variants.sad: A traveler speaks of loss on quiet nights; Arin listens and offers a steady shoulder before walking on alone.

callbacks.text: The smith's pendant catches the lantern light.

variants.neutral: A squall rolls in off the harbour; Arin braces against the rail as the lanterns sway and rain begins to fall.
variants.happy: Rain hammers the planks and Arin whoops into the wind, soaked and strangely delighted.
variants.uplift: Thunder cracks over the water and the whole bridge shudders; Arin runs, heart racing, toward the beam of the lighthouse.
variants.sad: The storm drives everyone indoors; Arin walks on alone through the rain, collar up, steady in the noise.

variants.neutral: Night falls and Arin walks toward a lighthouse on the headland, its beam rolling like a watchful eye.
variants.happy: At the top he looks out over the sea, laughing as the lights wink back like friends; the world feels wide and kind.
variants.uplift: An unexpected ship on the horizon flashes a signal; Arin senses that a journey is beginning.
variants.sad: He watches the tide pull at the shore and remembers things that ache; still, the lighthouse steadies him like a promise.

callbacks.text: The smith's pendant hums faintly in the beam.
He remembers the folktale's last line and finally understands it.

endings.text: Arin reaches the end of the day lighter than he began it; the whole coast glitters below him, and every friendly face has become a story he can't wait to tell.
Arin's pulse is still racing when the beam sweeps past; he does not want the day to end, and already the horizon is calling him toward the next adventure.
Arin stands quietly as the beam turns; the day was gentler than it was loud, and he leaves with a calm certainty that he will be all right.
Arin passes through town and beyond—every person met, every door opened, turns into a new story he carries forward.
